summary: Ghost, self-hosted properly: the open-source CMS in Docker with MySQL 8, Caddy for HTTPS, transactional email over SMTP, newsletters through Mailgun (the only bulk provider Ghost supports self-hosted), memberships wired to Stripe in test mode first, and a backup you have actually restored once. You save the subscription and take on upgrades and deliverability.

stack.why: rule zero: do not write a CMS
the only database Ghost supports in production; MariaDB and SQLite are not
Ghost's bulk sending is built on Mailgun's API specifically

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A VPS with at least 2 GB of RAM
prerequisites.why: Ghost plus MySQL need it. Ubuntu 24.04 with SSH.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner CX22 or a DigitalOcean 2 GB droplet.

prerequisites.name: Docker Engine and Compose on the VPS
prerequisites.why: Ghost and MySQL run as containers.
prerequisites.get: Follow docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu, then add your user to the docker group.
prerequisites.verify: docker compose version prints a version

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: Ghost's url setting must be the exact public HTTPS address.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: SMTP credentials for transactional mail
prerequisites.why: Password resets, staff invites and member sign-in links. Any SMTP provider.
prerequisites.get: Postmark, Fastmail or Mailgun's SMTP: host, port, username, password.

prerequisites.name: A Mailgun account, API key and sending domain
prerequisites.why: Newsletters will not send over SMTP. Ghost's bulk email is Mailgun-only for self-hosted installs as of 2026.
prerequisites.get: Sign up at mailgun.com, add a sending domain (mail.yourdomain.com), add the DNS records it shows (SPF, DKIM, MX), then Settings > API Keys > create a key. Verify current provider support in Ghost's docs before relying on this.

prerequisites.name: A Stripe account with test-mode keys
prerequisites.why: Paid memberships. Test mode first, live as a separate deliberate step.
prerequisites.get: dashboard.stripe.com > Developers > API keys (toggle Test mode). Ghost connects via Stripe Connect from its settings.
prerequisites.cost: free; fees per transaction when live

prerequisites.name: Somewhere off the box for backups
prerequisites.why: A backup on the server being backed up is not a backup.
prerequisites.get: Backblaze B2 or Cloudflare R2 bucket plus rclone configured on the VPS.

env.name: GHOST_URL
env.where: The exact public address. Wrong here means broken links and mixed content.

phases.title: Bring it up locally
phases.goal: Ghost and MySQL running from one compose file, data surviving a restart.

steps.do: Write docker-compose.yml with ghost and mysql:8
steps.detail: Named volumes for content and the database, health checks, restart: unless-stopped, every secret from .env.

steps.do: Start it and reach the setup screen

check: The site loads on localhost
/ghost reaches the admin setup screen
docker compose down && docker compose up -d preserves posts and settings
traps: MySQL 8.0 or 8.4 only. Substituting MariaDB or SQLite is a migration you discover at the worst moment.

phases.title: Domain and TLS
phases.goal: Public HTTPS, Ghost bound to localhost, url set correctly.

steps.do: Write the Caddyfile and set GHOST_URL
steps.detail: Your domain with reverse_proxy localhost:2368. Ghost's port published on 127.0.0.1 only.

steps.do: Point DNS and verify from another machine

check: HTTPS with a valid certificate; HTTP redirects
curl to the server IP on 2368 from outside is refused
No page shows a mixed-content warning

phases.title: Transactional email
phases.goal: Magic links and invites arrive in a real inbox.

steps.do: Set the mail__ environment variables from your SMTP provider and restart
steps.detail: mail__transport, mail__options__host, port, auth user and pass, mail__from.

steps.do: Send a staff invite and a member magic link and read both in a real inbox
steps.detail: Check the spam folder too; if they land there, fix SPF for the from domain before moving on.

check: A member magic link arrives
A staff invite arrives

phases.title: Newsletter delivery
phases.goal: Bulk email through Mailgun with DNS that keeps it out of spam.

steps.do: Add SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for the sending domain
steps.detail: Mailgun shows the exact records. DMARC starts at p=none.

steps.do: Enter the Mailgun API key and domain in Ghost's Email newsletter settings
Send a test newsletter to a Gmail and an Outlook address

check: The test newsletter reaches the inbox at a major provider, not spam
A mail-tester style check passes SPF, DKIM and DMARC
traps: Plain SMTP delivers your password resets and will not deliver your newsletter. These are two systems.

phases.title: Memberships and payments
phases.goal: Tiers and gating working in test mode before a single live key exists.

steps.do: Connect Stripe in test mode and create tiers
Run a test subscription and gate a post

check: A test-mode subscription completes and the member shows the right tier
A paid post is gated for a free member and readable for a paid one
Cancelling in Stripe revokes access

phases.title: Theme
phases.goal: The default theme adjusted, not a theme from scratch.

steps.do: Adjust the default theme's settings and upload any small CSS changes

check: Renders correctly on mobile
The theme survives docker compose restart

phases.title: Backup, and a restore drill
phases.goal: A nightly backup off the box and one restore you actually performed.

steps.do: Write backup.sh: mysqldump plus a tar of the content volume, to ./backups, fourteen kept, copied off the box
commands: docker compose exec -T mysql mysqldump -u root -p$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD ghost > backups/ghost-$(date +%F).sql
docker run --rm -v ghost_content:/c -v $PWD/backups:/b alpine tar czf /b/content-$(date +%F).tgz -C /c .

steps.do: Restore into a throwaway compose stack and check posts, members and images
steps.detail: Do this now, not later. Write the date in the README.

check: Last night's backup exists off the box
A restore into a clean stack brings up the site with posts, members and images intact
The restore date is written in the README

phases.title: Upgrades and handover
phases.goal: A repeatable upgrade and the honest trade written down.

steps.do: Write update.sh: backup, pull, up -d, verify

steps.detail: Every DNS record and what breaks without it, the restore date, and the trade: you now own upgrades, patching, deliverability and support.

check: One upgrade cycle has been run and the site is up
The README lists every DNS record

product.outcome: A publication platform you operate with confidence: monitored, backed up with a proven restore, upgradable in one command.

architecture.swap: It is the product; you do not fork it
Managed MySQL 8 later, same dump format
Any reverse proxy or a CDN in front

architecture.owns: SMTP for transactional, Mailgun for bulk
architecture.swap: SMTP provider freely; bulk provider only as Ghost adds support

operations.backup: Nightly mysqldump plus content tar, fourteen kept, copied off the box.
operations.restore: restore.sh into a clean stack; verified once already, re-verify after major upgrades.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on the homepage and /ghost/api/admin/site/; watch Mailgun's dashboard for bounces.
operations.incident: Deliverability drop: check DNS records and Mailgun suppressions. Compromise: rebuild from compose, restore, rotate every credential in .env and Stripe.

releaseGate: Newsletter test lands in the inbox at two major providers
One restore drill performed and dated
Stripe live keys enabled only after a test-mode subscription and cancellation succeeded

notIncluded: A custom theme from scratch and any custom blog engine code.
A CDN and WAF in front; worth adding later.
after: Cloudflare in front for caching and a WAF
A staging stack from last night's backup to test upgrades on
